_comment: NON-RUNNABLE INSTALLATION TEMPLATE for Kimi Code hooks. deploy/register-members.py renders it into ~/.kimi-code/config.toml as flat `[[hooks]] event = ...` tables (install.registration.layout = flat), reconciling by target: a line whose target is under the declared dest is hestia's and is rewritten to this template on every deploy (dp 2026-10-06); any other line is never touched. @HESTIA_HOME@ renders to the deploying environment's HESTIA_HOME as an absolute path, refused when unset (#1237); HESTIA_ROLE passes a launcher's value through and otherwise defaults to install.default_role. Unrendered placeholders must never be deployed.
_witness_note: witness.py is the hook that reaches the daemon; kimi fires PostToolUseFailure INSTEAD of PostToolUse for a failed call, so the witness is registered on both. Before 2026-09-28 kimi shipped no witness: its seat ran a private 07-26 copy of claude-code's that never saw a failure and never closed a gated action (findings/per-harness-witness-drift-2026-09-28.md).
_timeout_contract: One-gate stage C, critical-timeout protocol (#1262). The PreToolUse gate READS its timeout from the flat [[hooks]] table this template becomes (seconds). The value must be ONE explicit, structurally parsed timeout inside the canonical 3-30 s envelope: a missing, duplicate, unreadable or out-of-envelope timeout is MISWIRED and closes the bound — Kimi's documented 30 s vendor default is never substituted. The gate decides inside start + timeout - margin with margin = max(0.5, min(1.5, timeout*0.15)), so it always fails closed before Kimi kills it (Kimi's engine allows the tool on a timeout, i.e. fail-open). 15 s absorbs a cold member connect (measured 4.6-5.1 s). A registration outside the envelope is rejected, not clamped; deploy/register-members.py reports a noncanonical one. Nothing in this template sets HESTIA_PRE_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS: since stage C no gate reads it (the deadline is the registration's), so a hand-added one on a registered command is inert and should be removed.
